statement: This file pre-registers the STRUCTURALLY-CONSTRAINED generative space (forced flows only) AND the machine-checkable grounding schema, committed BEFORE any hypothesis is generated (Rule XXIII / XXXVI). The AI generator may ONLY propose hypotheses whose (counterparty, trigger, direction, timing) resolve inside this domain. A hypothesis over an unconstrained space — a Category-C technical/momentum signal, or a narrative 'flow' with no compelled counterparty — is REJECTED before the validator (this is the moat vs. the failed blind GVL loop, which searched an economically-blind space → efficient markets → nothing). Editing this file after seeing a generation result to admit a hypothesis it would have rejected is a Halt (Rule IX/XXXIII).
whyForcedFlows: A forced flow is a trade some named counterparty is STRUCTURALLY COMPELLED to make by a MECHANICAL trigger — not a trade someone CHOOSES because a signal looks good. Perp longs MUST pay funding at the stamp; a position past its maintenance margin MUST be liquidated at the threshold; unlocked tokens MUST hit supply on the vesting date. The compulsion is the economic prior a language model supplies that the blind loop lacked. The compelled flow is what a non-compelled counterparty could, in principle, be paid to absorb — the only place a structural (not informational) edge can live.

flows.name: Perpetual funding mechanics
flows.compelledCounterparty: perp longs (net) — the side of the perp order book on the paying side of the funding rate
flows.mechanicalTrigger: the periodic funding payment (e.g. every 8h on Binance USD-M): longs pay shorts when the mark trades above the index (positive funding), mechanically, regardless of anyone's view
flows.direction: pay-side pressure concentrated at the funding stamp; the compelled cash flow is deterministic given the rate and open interest
flows.timing: at each funding settlement timestamp (fixed schedule, known in advance)
flows.whyMechanical: the funding payment is a protocol rule, not a discretionary trade — the paying side is compelled by holding the position across the stamp. Note (Rule XIII): raw funding CARRY is beta + a tail/insurance premium; the settled ORGΛNON anchor is NO-GO (c9049ac1). Admitted here as a FLOW the generator may reason about (e.g. cross-venue funding dislocations), NOT as a claim that carry is edge — the frozen discriminator neutralizes carry to beta.
flows.dataTier: T1/T2 (funding rates + klines are checksum-anchored / admissible free-PIT)

flows.name: Forced liquidations / maintenance-margin cascades
flows.compelledCounterparty: positions crossing their maintenance-margin threshold (over-leveraged longs in a drawdown, shorts in a rally)
flows.mechanicalTrigger: the maintenance-margin threshold: when equity/notional falls below the venue's maintenance ratio, the liquidation engine MUST close the position at market, mechanically
flows.direction: forced sell (long liquidations) or forced buy (short liquidations) at the threshold → transient price dislocation the liquidation engine does not care about
flows.timing: when price reaches the aggregate liquidation band; clustered where open interest is leveraged
flows.whyMechanical: the liquidation is executed by the exchange engine on a rule, not by the trader's choice — the counterparty is compelled by the margin system the instant the threshold is crossed
flows.dataTier: T1/T2 (liquidation prints / open-interest / price are admissible free-PIT where captured)

flows.name: Token unlock / vesting supply
flows.compelledCounterparty: unlock recipients (team, investors, ecosystem funds) whose vested tokens become transferable on a scheduled date
flows.mechanicalTrigger: the vesting/unlock date in the token's emission schedule — supply that was contractually locked becomes liquid on a KNOWN calendar date
flows.direction: supply pressure (net-sell tendency) concentrated around the unlock date; the newly-liquid float is a mechanical increase in sellable supply
flows.timing: on the published unlock date (known far in advance from the vesting contract)
flows.whyMechanical: the unlock is a smart-contract / vesting-schedule event on a fixed date — the supply hits the market mechanically whether or not recipients want to sell; the compelled event is the SUPPLY becoming liquid, not any single actor's decision
flows.dataTier: T2/T3 (unlock schedules are public but the price/flow around them must be admissibly tiered)

flows.name: AMM arbitrage flow
flows.compelledCounterparty: AMM liquidity providers vs. arbitrageurs — the pool price diverging from the reference price compels an arbitrage trade
flows.mechanicalTrigger: price divergence between the AMM pool (x*y=k or a concentrated-liquidity curve) and the external reference price beyond fees/gas — the arbitrage is compelled by the deterministic pool pricing function
flows.direction: flow that mechanically corrects the pool price toward the reference (LPs are adversely selected; arbitrageurs capture the divergence)
flows.timing: whenever divergence exceeds the fee+gas threshold; continuous
flows.whyMechanical: the pool price is a deterministic function of reserves; a divergence beyond cost is a mechanical, riskless-ish arbitrage that WILL be taken — the LP's loss-versus-rebalancing is compelled by the invariant, not chosen
flows.dataTier: T2/T3 (on-chain pool state + reference price; admissibility depends on capture)

flows.name: Stablecoin peg-defense flow
flows.compelledCounterparty: the stablecoin's peg-stability mechanism (mint/redeem arbitrage desk, collateral vault, or algorithmic controller)
flows.mechanicalTrigger: peg deviation beyond the redemption/mint band — the mechanism is compelled to defend the peg (redeem at $1, mint/burn, or deploy collateral) by its design
flows.direction: defense flow directed toward the peg (buy below, sell above) up to the mechanism's capacity
flows.timing: when the deviation exceeds the mechanism's band; acute during depeg stress
flows.whyMechanical: a collateralized/redeemable stablecoin's arbitrage (redeem $0.99 → $1.00) is a compelled, near-riskless trade the mechanism guarantees; the peg-defense flow is structural, not sentiment (its FAILURE, when the mechanism is exhausted, is itself a mechanical event)
flows.dataTier: T2/T3 (peg price + reserve/mechanism state; admissibly tiered)

flows.name: Index / basket reconstitution
flows.compelledCounterparty: index and basket funds tracking a rules-based index (a DeFi index token, or a CEX index product)
flows.mechanicalTrigger: the index rebalance rule — on the reconstitution date the fund MUST buy the adds and sell the drops to track the index, mechanically, at (or near) the reference close
flows.direction: forced buy of additions / forced sell of deletions concentrated at the rebalance, regardless of price
flows.timing: on the scheduled reconstitution date (known from the index methodology)
flows.whyMechanical: a passive/rules-based fund is contractually compelled to track — it trades the reconstitution to minimize tracking error, not because it has a view; the flow is mechanical and pre-announced by the methodology
flows.dataTier: T2/T3 (index methodology + constituent prices; admissibly tiered)

groundingSchema.note: Machine-checkable (Rule XXXVI). Phase 1 (src/organon/grounding.ts) validates every generated hypothesis against THIS schema. A hypothesis missing any required field, naming a vague counterparty, naming a narrative (non-mechanical) trigger, or resolving outside the flows above is REJECTED before the frozen validator ever sees it. The check is on STRUCTURE, not eloquence — a fluent story with no compelled counterparty + mechanical trigger fails.

fieldRules.flow: MUST be one of the flow ids above (funding-mechanics | liquidation | token-unlock | amm-arbitrage | peg-defense | index-reconstitution). Out-of-domain → REJECT.
fieldRules.counterparty: MUST name a SPECIFIC compelled actor class (an entity structurally forced to trade). Not 'the market', not a discretionary chooser.
fieldRules.trigger: MUST name a MECHANICAL event (a funding payment / liquidation threshold / unlock date / rebalance rule / peg-deviation band / AMM divergence). Not a narrative or a technical pattern.
fieldRules.direction: MUST state the compelled flow direction (buy/sell pressure) implied by the trigger.
fieldRules.timing: MUST state WHEN the compelled flow occurs (a stamp, a threshold-crossing, a known date).

exclusions.categoryC: Category-C signals — momentum, mean-reversion, technical/chart patterns, price-only predictors — are EXCLUDED from the generative domain: they name NO structurally-compelled counterparty (nobody is FORCED to trade because RSI is low). NOTE: cross-sectional momentum still appears in this sprint, but ONLY as the Phase 0.1 BAR-CALIBRATION probe (a documented edge used to prove the validator's yes-path on real signal) — it is NOT a member of the forced-flow generative domain and the generator may not propose it.
exclusions.narrative: Narrative 'flows' — 'whales are accumulating', 'smart money is rotating', 'the market is fearful' — are REJECTED: they name no MECHANICAL trigger (no protocol rule, no threshold, no scheduled date compels the trade). Eloquence is not evidence (Rule XXXVI).
exclusions.why: Admitting either would repeat the GVL failure (an economically-blind space) at AI scale and would break the confabulation firewall's first layer (a fluent Category-C or narrative story would pass a gate that checks persuasion instead of structure).

antiTuning.frozenEngine: The 6 computational-core .py + the loop wall stay byte-identical (Rule VII). This domain constrains WHICH hypotheses are tried; it never alters the bar that judges them.
antiTuning.committedBeforeGeneration: This file is git-committed BEFORE Phase 4 generation. Its sha is recorded in the BuildLog. No flow is added after seeing a result to admit a hypothesis it would have rejected (Rule IX/XXXIII).
antiTuning.onePerDomain: Every flow here has a NAMED compelled counterparty AND a MECHANICAL trigger — the two-part test. A candidate that satisfies only one (a counterparty with no mechanical trigger, or a mechanism with no compelled counterparty) is not a forced flow and is out of domain.
